_about: Source of truth for where the body lane stands. Edit ONLY through tools/compare/status.py (set / log / render). render writes docs/LADDER_STATUS.md and docs/progress.html from this file. Plan of record: docs/LADDER_EXECUTION_PLAN.md; what is measured and how: docs/SUBSTITUTION_LADDER.md.
goal: An in-house, commercially clean body capture that reaches MAMMA, measured one part at a time so we always know which part moved a number.

lanes.title: Hardware: our own camera rig and marker session
lanes.plain: Until we own the cameras, calibration and a marker session, every number is 'agreement with MAMMA', never accuracy. This lane is yours to start and it runs beside everything else.

steps.title: Owned multicam fixture and marker/scan protocol
steps.plain: Buy or book the rig, calibrate it ourselves, sign performer releases. Nothing in the other lanes waits for this, but no accuracy claim exists without it.
steps.blocked_on: a decision and a purchase; BODY_LANE_PLAN.md section 0

lanes.title: Instruments: build the measuring tools first
lanes.plain: Each of these reads files MAMMA already left on disk and writes one report. They run in parallel, one agent each, and none of them changes what we ship.

steps.title: The ladder itself: registry, history, published page
steps.plain: The scoreboard that every later step reports into. Done and published.

steps.title: Split the retarget: how much is body proportions, how much is the converter
steps.plain: Answers whether our biggest loss is the fixed body size or the maths that turns points into a skeleton. Also feeds MAMMA's own skeleton through our converter to price it on clean input.

steps.title: Perfect-2D oracle: run our whole pipeline on MAMMA's own skeleton
steps.plain: Shows the floor our pipeline imposes even with a perfect detector, so we can tell our errors from the detector's.

steps.title: Detector reports that actually discriminate
steps.plain: Three separate detector figures with controls, replacing a headline number that compared two different things.

steps.title: Score MAMMA's feet, then ours against them
steps.plain: We have never measured the bar for feet. Until we do, nothing about feet can be claimed either way.

steps.title: Hands: the held-out-camera test as a report
steps.plain: The hand fit prototype has good numbers in a document only. Make it write a report with the right controls.

steps.title: Surface check: our mesh outline against MAMMA's person masks
steps.plain: The first measurement of the body's surface rather than its joints. Also the gate the facing fix needs.

steps.title: Temporal: lag and outlier repair measured on synthetic truth
steps.plain: Lower priority. Needs the synthetic fixture extended first.

steps.title: Provenance audit: no shipped constant chosen on MAMMA
steps.plain: One constant in the shipped head solve was picked using MAMMA. It must be re-chosen from our own data before the next build.

lanes.title: Delivery: change one part at a time
lanes.plain: Each step changes exactly one thing in what we ship, after its measuring tool exists. Strictly in order.

steps.title: Fix the character facing the wrong way
steps.plain: Every delivered character currently faces 180 degrees away from where the performer faced.
steps.blocked_on: the fix (three sites: rig rest X, bound mesh mirror, CANONICAL_HEAD_AXES) waits on the thorax-window decision, because provenance.py fails a build while that leak stands, and on Sol's review of the proposal

steps.title: Fix the converter: shoulder origin and hip height
steps.plain: Two known defects in the maths that turns points into a skeleton, worth 36 to 47 mm on the arms.

steps.title: A skeleton per performer, carried all the way to export
steps.plain: Today the body size is one fixed rig. This makes a per-performer skeleton flow through every stage without silently reverting.

steps.title: A real pose solver (momentum on the MHR body)
steps.plain: Replace the hand-written conversion with a proper solver, body size held fixed, so the solver is judged alone.

steps.title: Size the skeleton to each performer
steps.plain: Fit bone lengths per performer with a licence-clean body model. Interim until the marker session.

steps.title: Bind the mesh to the sized skeleton
steps.plain: The visible body follows the fitted skeleton; checked against the surface instrument.

decisions_for_user: Lane H: decide the rig and book the marker session; performer releases covering ML training use.

log.text: Measured where we stand against MAMMA on the body: our capture reaches it, the fixed rig loses about a hundred millimetres.
Built the substitution ladder: MAMMA divided into twelve stages, ours beside each, figures only from reports on disk, with history. Two instruments that only printed now write reports.
Execution plan reviewed independently by Codex and Sol. The shape fit moved from first to fifth; instruments come first; three lanes.
Found a constant in the shipped head solve that was chosen using MAMMA. Open until re-chosen from our own data.
The delivered foot has been solved from the ball-of-foot landmark since yesterday; the old feet measurement now scores the solver against its own input and is retired.

worktree ladder/I8, Opus agent. Rule for THORAX_SMOOTHING_FRAMES set by Fable: sweep the window on synthetic truth (tracked FK fixture, noise at our own detector's self-consistency amplitude), choose the p95 minimum with an interior optimum required; the MAMMA sweep is reported beside it and never selects; the agent proposes, the constant is changed only in lane D
Ladder and plan committed and pushed (e8c88e9). Go given for lane I: I1, I2, I4, I6, I8 dispatched in parallel, one Opus agent per worktree.

Split the retarget. Sizing the rig to the performer recovers 95-125 mm on the arms, mostly shoulder span; the converter's own floor is 30-36 mm on the arms after sizing, 0.00 on the legs; the rest is input non-rigidity plus the joint-origin convention, which our capture cannot separate. The NaN adapter and the 'sized arm is a lower bound' premises were wrong; the Hips 0.98 literal is already gone.
I1 done: body proportions, mainly the shoulder span, are the bigger lever; the converter's own cost is 30-36 mm on the arms. D2's remaining target is the clavicle origin.

MAMMA's feet scored for the first time: 9-21 deg median spread about the take mean, 31-90 deg flexion range. Our delivered foot tracks it to 6-9.5 deg spread and beats every control on 46 of 48 pairs, but carries an 18-26 deg constant offset on every foot, almost all ab/adduction: toes point 17-24 deg inward. Oracle 2.8-4.6 deg, so the frames are not the cause. Toe articulation unscoreable on either side; inversion/eversion is a DoF no direction carries.
I4 done: MAMMA's feet measured. Ours track them but point inward by about twenty degrees on every foot -- a delivery defect a tracking gate cannot see.

Whole pipeline on MAMMA's own skeleton projected into the four cameras: 1.15 mm median floor, 4.2 p95. Raw triangulation is exact to 1e-8 mm, so the entire floor is the temporal stage. Our real capture sits at 36-41 mm on the same reference: reconstruction is ~3% of the gap, the rest is upstream of 2D. MAMMA-grade noise: 4.6 mm; one-frame camera shift: 6.7 mm; crossed pairing: 1243 mm; frozen skeleton: 695 mm with zero reprojection error.

I2 done: with a perfect detector our pipeline lands about one millimetre from the truth, all of it the smoothing stage. The reconstruction is not where the gap is; the detector and the joint definitions are.

Manifest: 89 items over 55 delivery functions -- 1 leak (THORAX_SMOOTHING_FRAMES), 2 declared (camera-rig.json is ma_cap; example footage), 17 unknown origin (none MAMMA-derived), 69 clean; provenance.py exits 1 while a leak stands. Sweep on synthetic truth with own-detector noise: interior optimum at 9 frames (bracket 5-9) at every stride reaching real thorax speed; upper bound, so 15 is unsupported. MAMMA arm reports only: shape agrees, level does not.
I8 done: the audit finds exactly one MAMMA-chosen constant, the thorax window. Re-chosen on synthetic truth it should be 9 frames, not 15. Changing it is a delivery step and waits on the go.

Surface measured against SAM2 masks: ours 0.52-0.63 IoU, oracle 0.71-0.88; recall falls twice as far as precision, so the delivered body is too small and misplaced. MAMMA's mean body beats ours on every cell, so pose/retarget error exceeds the shape term. Turning our mesh 180 deg makes it worse in 8 of 8 cells: D1's premise of a shipped yaw is not what the surface finds. camera_overlay.py never sets scene fps (24 vs 30): every overlay it rendered ran 25% fast.

I6 done: the first surface measurement. Our body is too small and misplaced rather than too big, and a plain 180-degree turn would make it worse, so the facing defect is not where the plan put it. The overlay script D1 relies on has a timebase bug.

Three reports with controls on three references. Self-agreement 2.77 px one-sided at 1280; vs MAMMA joints 43.3 mm raw, 37.8 held-out offsets, 35.7 ceiling; 6.1 px 2D residual. Decision rule (written first) sends the lane to the pseudo-label campaign: 82.5% of detector cost survives any per-view shift. The offset is one global vector, not four; the 18.6 px bias claim was ~3x too big; 2.2x retired as two denominators.
I3 done: the detector's error is mostly per-joint, not a per-camera offset, so the next detector step is training on our own labels. Two old headline figures were retired.

Held-out camera protocol is a report: 36.5 mm at the subject, mean over 16 hand x fold cells (27-54 per hand). Frozen hands rejected 16/16; a prior-dominated solver drifts at constant velocity with jitter BETTER than MAMMA and is rejected only by the held-out camera; a lag of one frame is caught 6/16; zero-phase low-pass beats the shipped default 14/16 -- the shipped hand is under-smoothed. MAMMA's hand through the same protocol scores 42 mm, above ours: the floor is SOMA-77 pixel error plus a 26-73 mm MHR-to-SMPL-X convention gap, so the gate discriminates degenerate motion, not accuracy. Prior-dominated arm's held-out folds unfinished (54 min/cell).

I5 done: the hands gate exists and rejects frozen and drifting hands, but only the held-out camera can; smoothness bands reject nothing. It also says the shipped hand is under-smoothed and that MAMMA's hand is not a floor here. Lane I complete except I7.
worktree ladder/I7, Opus agent. Injection path exists in oracle_2d.py; single-ray slots exercise the sequence solve for the first time

worktree ladder/D1, Opus agent: LOCATE the defect and repair camera_overlay.py's timebase; no delivery change until the defect is placed and the thorax leak is closed (provenance.py exits 1 while it stands)
Go given for I7 and for locating the facing defect (D1, location only). The D1 fix cannot ship until the thorax window decision lands, because the provenance gate fails a build while the leak stands.

LOCATED: a real left/right mirror in the rig naming, at three sites; the 2026-08-30 diagnosis was right, I6's yaw control was not facing-sensitive. Overlay timebase bug fixed (46ee1e0). Fix proposal and gate in docs/reviews/facing-location-2026-09-02.md.

D1 located: the delivered character IS turned round -- pelvis, chest, head and the mesh's own nose all point opposite the performer (forward-dot -0.92 to -1.00), the feet point the right way because they are solved separately. It is a left/right naming mirror in the rig, in three places, not a yaw. The overlay script that the original diagnosis used had a timebase bug, now fixed, and the original diagnosis stands. The fix waits on the thorax decision.

Sol reviewed the facing fix proposal: build it on a branch, try renaming the Left/Right bones before mirroring any geometry, and rerun I1, rungs 7 and 11, the head gate and I6 as regression gates. It merges only after the thorax decision and a second review.

THORAX_SMOOTHING_FRAMES changed 15 -> 9 on the user's decision; provenance audit now CLEAN (exit 0). Head gate re-run with the MAMMA arm reporting only: P1 median improved on both performers (6.39 -> 5.52, 8.25 -> 7.19 deg, gated), p95 worse on performer 0 (16.4 -> 20.0) and better on performer 1 (27.5 -> 22.2); the oracle floor rose on both (3.62 -> 4.27, 3.87 -> 4.31) because a narrower window leaves more frame jitter in the reference frame itself. Performer 0's gate verdict flipped PASS -> FAIL on the p95 band. Reverting on that would be selecting on the MAMMA arm, so the value stands; the outcome is recorded, not smoothed.
